import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer

def categorical_imputation():
    # Create mixed-type DataFrame with missing values
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        'city': ['NYC', 'LA', np.nan, 'NYC', np.nan, 'Chicago', 'LA', 'NYC'],
        'department': ['Engineering', np.nan, 'Sales', 'Engineering', 'Marketing', np.nan, 'Sales', 'Engineering'],
        'experience': [5, np.nan, 3, 8, np.nan, 2, 6, 10],
        'has_car': [True, np.nan, False, True, np.nan, False, True, np.nan]
    })
    
    print("Original DataFrame:")
    print(df)
    
    # Mode imputation
    mode_imputer = SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent')
    df_mode = pd.DataFrame(
        mode_imputer.fit_transform(df),
        columns=df.columns
    )
    
    print("\nMode (Most Frequent) Imputation:")
    print(df_mode)
    
    # Constant value imputation
    const_imputer_num = SimpleImputer(strategy='constant', fill_value=0)
    df_exp_const = pd.DataFrame(
        const_imputer_num.fit_transform(df[['experience']]),
        columns=['experience']
    )
    
    const_imputer_cat = SimpleImputer(strategy='constant', fill_value='Unknown')
    df_city_const = pd.DataFrame(
        const_imputer_cat.fit_transform(df[['city']]),
        columns=['city']
    )
    
    print("\nConstant Imputation (experience=0, city='Unknown'):")
    result = df.copy()
    result['experience'] = df_exp_const['experience']
    result['city'] = df_city_const['city']
    print(result)

categorical_imputation()
